headline: Regional Parking Permits and Seasonal Road Access
reservation: Access to local trails and state parks near Wenatchee requires a Discover Pass or Northwest Forest Pass depending on the specific land manager. While the city parks are open access, boat launches and specialized recreation sites may require a local fee; check the official Wenatchee city or USFS sites for current requirements.

days.title: Riverfront Vistas and Local Flavors
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from Pybus Public Market

stops.name: Apple Capital Recreation Loop Trail
stops.detail: Cycle or walk this 10-mile paved path for continuous views of the Columbia River.

stops.name: Pybus Public Market
stops.detail: Sample regional agricultural products and local crafts in a restored historic warehouse.

days.driving: Walking or cycling is sufficient for the loop; local transfers are under 10 minutes.
days.note: The river breeze can be cool in the morning; layers are suggested for the Loop Trail.

days.title: High Desert Heights and Alpine Blooms
days.start: Suggested: 7:30 AM from Saddle Rock Trailhead

stops.name: Saddle Rock
stops.detail: Climb the twin peaks for a 360-degree panorama of the Wenatchee Valley and the Cascades.

stops.name: Ohme Gardens
stops.detail: Explore a lush hillside oasis featuring stone paths, waterfalls, and panoramic valley overlooks.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes between the desert foothills and the garden bluffs.
days.note: Saddle Rock offers no shade; early morning starts are essential during the summer months.

days.title: River Confluence and Cultural Heritage
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Confluence State Park

stops.name: Confluence State Park
stops.detail: Enjoy the swimming beach where the Wenatchee and Columbia rivers meet.

stops.name: Wenatchee Valley Museum & Cultural Center
stops.detail: Learn about the region's apple industry and railroad history through interactive exhibits.

days.driving: Allow 25 minutes for the drive to EAT airport; traffic is typically light.
days.note: Check current river flow and temperature before swimming; currents can be deceptively strong.

intel.title: Trailhead Passes
intel.text: Parking at Saddle Rock is free but fills quickly on weekend mornings; arrive early for a spot. Confluence State Park requires a Discover Pass, which can be purchased at automated kiosks in the park.

intel.title: Urban vs. Wilderness
intel.text: Cellular coverage is excellent within the Wenatchee city limits and along the Loop Trail. Signal drops rapidly as you drive deeper into the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest to the west.

intel.title: Valley Hub
intel.text: Wenatchee is the primary fueling station for the region; ensure your tank is full before heading toward Stevens Pass. Electric vehicle chargers are increasingly available near Pybus Market and downtown hotels.

intel.title: Fruit Bloom and Harvest
intel.text: Late April is the peak for apple blossoms, while harvest season brings a bustle to the valley in September. If visiting for the Apple Blossom Festival, plan for significantly higher foot traffic downtown.

intel.title: Seasonal Burn Bans
intel.text: The arid summer climate often leads to strict seasonal burn bans; check the official county fire marshal site before planning a campfire. Some lower foothills trails may close in early spring to protect muddy paths.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at EAT airport, take the 20-minute drive to the riverfront for check-in and an initial walk on the Loop Trail.
plan.vehicle: A standard passenger vehicle is suitable for the city and main sights; high-clearance is only needed for remote USFS roads.
plan.goldenHour: Ohme Gardens for sunset views over the Columbia River, though closing hours vary by month.
